tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Locate files in the codebase.

tools.name: grep_content
tools.description: Search inside file contents for a regex or literal pattern. Returns matching lines with surrounding context across the project.

pattern.description: Regex or literal text to match line-by-line

path.description: Optional directory or file path to restrict the search

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read the full contents of a file at the given path. Returns the file's text as a single string.

tools.name: head_file
tools.description: Return only the first N lines of a file. Useful for sampling large files without loading them entirely into memory.

lines.description: Number of leading lines to return

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List the immediate children (files and subdirectories) of a directory. Non-recursive; one level only.

tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Recursively walk a directory tree and return paths matching an optional glob pattern. Honors .gitignore.

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Show the working tree status: staged, unstaged, and untracked changes in the current repository.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Show line-level differences between the working tree and the index, or between two specified revisions.

ref.description: Optional revision or revision range, e.g. 'HEAD~3..HEAD'

tools.name: git_log
tools.description: Show the commit history of the current branch, including author, date, and commit message for each commit.

limit.description: Maximum number of commits to return

tools.name: git_commit
tools.description: Record a new commit with the staged changes and the supplied commit message. Fails if there are no staged changes.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Execute a single command without a shell and return stdout, stderr, and the exit code. No pipes, no globbing, no shell expansion.

argv.description: Command and its arguments as a list

tools.name: exec_in_terminal
tools.description: Run a command through a full shell so pipes, redirections, globs, and environment-variable expansion all work as expected.

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Make an HTTP GET request to a URL and return the response body as text. Follows redirects.

tools.name: http_request
tools.description: Make an arbitrary HTTP request with configurable method, headers, and body. Returns status code, response headers, and body.

method.description: HTTP method, e.g. GET, POST, PUT

tools.name: download_file
tools.description: Download a file from a URL to a local path. Streams large files to disk without loading them into memory.

destination.description: Local file path to write to

tools.name: find_symbol
tools.description: Locate a code symbol (function, class, variable) by name across the project. Returns the defining file path and line number.

tools.name: find_references
tools.description: Find all usage sites of a given symbol across the project. Returns file paths and line numbers for every reference.

name.description: Symbol name whose references to enumerate

tools.name: rename_symbol
tools.description: Rename a symbol across every file in the project, updating both its definition and all references atomically.

tools.name: format_file
tools.description: Auto-format a file according to the project's configured formatter (e.g. black for Python, prettier for JavaScript).

tools.name: compute_sha256
tools.description: Compute the SHA-256 hex digest of a file at the given path. Useful for content integrity checks and cache keys.
